rounds.t: Pituitary, adrenal zones, and pancreatic islets

q.s: A 30-year-old woman has headaches, amenorrhea and galactorrhea. MRI shows a sellar mass arising from the adenohypophysis. From which embryologic tissue does this part of the pituitary derive?
e: Endoderm forms gut-derived glands such as thyroid follicles and pancreas.
Mesoderm forms the adrenal cortex.
Neural crest forms the adrenal medulla.
Correct. The anterior pituitary derives from oral ectoderm via Rathke pouch.
Neuroectoderm forms the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis).

q.s: Which hormone is NOT secreted by the anterior pituitary?
e: Correct. Oxytocin is made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary.
TSH is an anterior pituitary basophil hormone.
Prolactin is secreted by anterior pituitary acidophils.
ACTH is secreted by anterior pituitary basophils.
GH is secreted by anterior pituitary acidophils.

q.s: Vasopressin and oxytocin are synthesized in which location?
o: Supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus
e: The pineal gland makes melatonin.
The arcuate nucleus makes dopamine and GHRH.
Correct. ADH and oxytocin are made in hypothalamic nuclei and carried to the posterior pituitary by neurophysins.
The posterior pituitary stores and releases them but does not synthesize them.
The anterior pituitary does not make these hormones.

q.s: The carrier proteins that transport ADH and oxytocin down axons to the posterior pituitary are called:
e: Transcortin (CBG) binds cortisol in plasma.
Thyroglobulin is the thyroid hormone storage protein.
Correct. Neurophysins carry ADH and oxytocin from hypothalamic nuclei to the posterior pituitary.
Synaptophysin is a synaptic vesicle protein used as a neuroendocrine marker.
Chromogranin is a marker of neuroendocrine secretory granules.

q.s: A woman has a positive urine pregnancy test, but the lab notes that a nonspecific assay could cross-react with LH, FSH and TSH. Which shared feature explains the cross-reactivity?
o: They share a common α subunit; the β subunit confers specificity
They are all derived from POMC
They are all secreted by acidophils
They all bind the same receptor
e: Correct. TSH, LH, FSH and hCG share the α subunit; the β subunit determines specificity, so specific tests measure β-hCG.
POMC gives ACTH, MSH and β-endorphin.
TSH, LH and FSH are basophil products; hCG is placental.
These are glycoprotein hormones, not steroids.
Each has a distinct receptor.

q.s: Proopiomelanocortin (POMC) is the precursor of which group of hormones?
e: These are hypothalamic releasing hormones.
These are glycoproteins sharing an α subunit.
These are hypothalamic nonapeptides.
Correct. POMC yields β-endorphin, ACTH and MSH ("go pro with a BAM").
These are structurally related but not POMC derivatives.

q.s: A pituitary section is stained with H&E. Which pair of hormones is made by acidophilic (eosinophilic) cells?
e: These are POMC products of basophils and the intermediate lobe.
These come from basophils.
These are released from the posterior pituitary, which is neural tissue.
These come from basophils.
Correct. "Acid PiG": acidophils make PRL and GH.

q.s: Which anterior pituitary hormones are produced by basophils?
e: These are acidophil hormones.
These come from the thyroid and parathyroid.
Correct. "B-FLAT": basophils make FSH, LH, ACTH and TSH.
ACTH is one of four basophil hormones.
These come from the hypothalamus via the posterior pituitary.

q.s: Melanotropin (MSH) is secreted mainly from which part of the pituitary?
e: The median eminence is the hypothalamic site of releasing-hormone secretion into portal blood.
Correct. MSH is secreted from the intermediate lobe of the pituitary.
The pars nervosa is the posterior pituitary.
The pars tuberalis wraps the infundibulum and is not the main MSH source.
The infundibulum is the pituitary stalk.

q.s: The posterior pituitary derives from which embryologic tissue?
e: Endoderm forms thyroid follicles and pancreatic islets.
Mesoderm forms the adrenal cortex.
Oral ectoderm forms the anterior pituitary.
Correct. The neurohypophysis is a downgrowth of the diencephalon (neuroectoderm).
Neural crest forms the adrenal medulla.

q.s: A 52-year-old man has hypertension and hypokalemia. Imaging shows an adrenal adenoma arising from the outermost zone of the cortex. What is the main physiologic regulator of this zone?
e: ACTH is the main regulator of the fasciculata and reticularis.
TSH regulates the thyroid.
These regulate the medulla.
Correct. The zona glomerulosa, which makes aldosterone, is regulated mainly by angiotensin II (and K+).
CRH acts on the pituitary to release ACTH.

q.s: Which adrenal zone produces cortisol?
e: Correct. The zona fasciculata produces glucocorticoids (cortisol) under ACTH and CRH control.
The glomerulosa makes aldosterone.
The reticularis makes androgens (DHEA).
The medulla makes catecholamines.
The capsule is connective tissue and makes no hormones.

q.s: A useful mnemonic for the adrenal cortex layers from outside in is "GFR = salt, sugar, sex." Which hormone corresponds to the innermost cortical layer?
e: Epinephrine comes from the medulla, deep to the cortex.
Correct. The zona reticularis ("sex") makes androgens such as DHEA.
Aldosterone ("salt") is from the outermost glomerulosa.
Norepinephrine is a medullary catecholamine.
Cortisol ("sugar") is from the middle fasciculata.

q.s: A 2-year-old has an abdominal mass arising from adrenal chromaffin cells. From which embryologic tissue do these cells derive?
e: Mesoderm forms the adrenal cortex.
Correct. The adrenal medulla (chromaffin cells) derives from neural crest, the origin of neuroblastoma and pheochromocytoma.
That forms the posterior pituitary.
Oral ectoderm forms the anterior pituitary.
Endoderm forms gut-derived glands.

q.s: Secretion of epinephrine from the adrenal medulla is directly triggered by:
e: Angiotensin II regulates the glomerulosa.
ACTH regulates the cortex, not catecholamine release.
The parasympathetic system does not drive medullary release.
K+ stimulates aldosterone release, not epinephrine.
Correct. Chromaffin cells act like postganglionic neurons and are stimulated by preganglionic sympathetic (cholinergic) fibers.

q.s: Which statement about adrenal embryology is correct?
o: The cortex derives from mesoderm and the medulla from neural crest
Both cortex and medulla derive from neural crest
The medulla derives from oral ectoderm
e: The medulla is not mesodermal.
Correct. Adrenal cortex is mesodermal; medulla is neural crest.
Only the medulla is neural crest.
The cortex is mesodermal.
Oral ectoderm forms the anterior pituitary.

q.s: In the islets of Langerhans, insulin-secreting cells are typically located:
o: At the periphery of the islet
In the center of the islet
e: δ cells are the interspersed population.
Peripheral cells are mainly α cells (glucagon).
Acini are exocrine and secrete enzymes.
Islets are separate from the duct system.
Correct. β cells (insulin) are central; α cells are peripheral; δ cells are interspersed.

q.s: A 58-year-old man has migratory necrolytic erythema and new diabetes. A tumor of which islet cell type is most likely, and where are these cells located in a normal islet?
e: δ-cell tumors (somatostatinomas) cause diabetes, gallstones and steatorrhea, not necrolytic migratory erythema.
β cells are central and make insulin.
β-cell tumors (insulinomas) cause hypoglycemia.
α cells are peripheral.
Correct. Glucagonoma arises from α cells, which sit at the islet periphery.

q.s: Which islet cell secretes somatostatin?
e: α cells secrete glucagon.
Ductal cells secrete bicarbonate.
Correct. δ cells secrete somatostatin and are interspersed through the islet.
β cells secrete insulin.
Acinar cells secrete digestive enzymes.

q.s: Pancreatic islets develop from which embryologic structure?
e: Correct. Islets arise from the pancreatic buds (foregut endoderm).
Rathke pouch forms the anterior pituitary.
Neural crest forms the adrenal medulla.
The septum transversum forms part of the diaphragm and liver stroma.
The urogenital ridge forms gonads and the adrenal cortex region.
